METR software-task time-horizon evaluation protocol

benchmark.metr-time-horizon

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

The original primary paper specifies a composite human-time-calibrated evaluation protocol, and the captured creator TH1.1 report explicitly documents a revised reusable setup applied to newer models. Separate identity review supports a composite evaluation-protocol lineage. HCAST, RE-Bench and SWAA are input collections, not evidence of independent task-data origin for this protocol. TH1 and TH1.1, model cohorts, success thresholds, scaffolds and dashboard plots remain versions/configurations in this one lineage. Overlapping inputs and hybrid reused estimates are not independent replication; no execution or current-performance assessment is asserted. Actual author, separate source-verifier and adversarial source-content review records bind every approved claim at its exact scientific digest. This metadata classification does not freeze core eligibility.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

METR software-task time-horizon evaluation protocol · documents: The TH1.1 release reports a post-2023 time-horizon doubling estimate of 130.8 days versus 165.3 days for TH1, using model sets that overlap substantially but are not identical.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.time-horizon.th11-growth-comparability.v2

  • No pre-2023 models were re-estimated with TH1.1; the approximately 196-day all-period TH1.1 comparison is a hybrid fit that retains TH1 estimates for earlier models.
  • The creator describes task-distribution changes and substantial overlap between old and new tasks; comparing these estimates does not provide an independent task-sample replication.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

METR software-task time-horizon evaluation protocol · documents: TH1.1 moves evaluation infrastructure from Vivaria to Inspect and re-estimates horizons for 14 of the 33 models with TH1 estimates.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.time-horizon.th11-model-and-infrastructure-coverage.v1

  • The creator lists model availability, required scaffold changes and distance from the release-time frontier as reasons for not re-estimating the other models.
  • Two named models, GPT-4-32k-0314 and o1-preview, used the new tasks on the old Vivaria infrastructure before being deprecated.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

METR software-task time-horizon evaluation protocol · documents: The TH1.1 creator compared Vivaria and Inspect using five models on the old TH1 tasks, and a separate three-model comparison on the new task suite.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.time-horizon.th11-scaffold-comparison.v1

  • On the old-task comparison, paired tests across task scores found higher Vivaria performance for GPT-4o and o3; the creator describes the new-suite three-model horizon differences as minor.
  • Reported horizon confidence intervals bootstrap task families, tasks and runs, so the creator cautions they overestimate run-level variance in the platform comparison.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

METR software-task time-horizon evaluation protocol · documents: The captured TH1.1 creator release changes the time-horizon suite from 170 to 228 tasks by adding 73 HCAST tasks and removing 15, while updating 53 existing tasks.

Permanent record ID: candidate.next8.metr.time-horizon.th11-task-version.v1

  • Of the 53 updates, 27 change task definitions, 13 change human-time estimates, and 13 change both; revisions and removals address issues such as confusing descriptions, reward hacking and scoring errors.
  • Tasks estimated at eight hours or more increase from 14 to 31, but only five of those 31 long tasks have measured human baseline times; the rest use estimated times.
